title: How Do You Give Your Accountant Access to QuickBooks Online?
summary: How to give your accountant access to QuickBooks Online: the exact steps, who can invite, accountant user limits, what your accountant can see, and how to fix a missing Accounting Firms tab.
body_markdown:
**To give your accountant access to QuickBooks Online, sign in as the primary admin, go to Settings, open Manage Users, select the Accounting Firms tab, enter your accountant's email, and send the invite.** They accept by email, and their status changes from Invited to Active. The whole thing takes a few minutes.


This guide covers the exact steps, who's allowed to invite, how many accountants you can add, what they can see, and how to fix the most common issue: a missing Accounting Firms tab.


## Key takeaways


- Only the primary admin (or a company admin) can invite an accountant.
- Accountant users are added under the Accounting Firms tab, not as regular users.
- Accountant users do not count against your plan's user limit.
- QuickBooks Online allows up to two accountant users on most plans, three on Advanced.
- QuickBooks Solopreneur can't invite an accountant; you must upgrade to Simple Start or higher.


## Why accountant access is a separate user type


QuickBooks treats accountants differently from regular users on purpose. An accountant user gets tools a standard user never sees, including the ability to undo reconciliations, reclassify transactions in batches, and write off invoices.


That's why you don't add your accountant as a normal team member. The accountant role unlocks the[accountant toolbox](https://www.finlens.app/guides/quickbooks-online-accountant-guide) they need to actually work in your books, and it comes with permissions built for financial professionals.


The other reason to use the dedicated role is cost. Accountant users don't count toward the user limit on your plan, so inviting one never forces a plan upgrade.


## How to add an accountant to QuickBooks Online


The process is short, but the order and the login role matter. Follow these steps exactly.


1. **Sign in as the primary admin.** Only the primary admin or a company admin can invite an accountant. If you're signed in as a standard user, you won't see the option.
2. **Open Settings.** Click the gear icon in the top right corner of QuickBooks Online.
3. **Select Manage Users.** This opens the list of everyone with access to your company file.
4. **Choose the Accounting Firms tab.** This tab is separate from the regular Users tab and is specifically for accountants and bookkeepers.
5. **Select Invite.** Enter your accountant's email address carefully. A typo here means the invite never arrives.
6. **Send the invite.** QuickBooks emails your accountant a link to accept. Their status shows as Invited until they do.
7. **Confirm they're active.** Once they accept and set up their login, their status changes from Invited to Active. Most accountants accept within a day.


That's the entire process. Your accountant now has access to your books through QuickBooks Online Accountant.[Intuit's official invite documentation](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/accountant-access/invite-accountant-review-accounting-quickbooks/L4ba0qT8r_US_en_US) mirrors these steps if you want the source.


## What your accountant can see and do


Once active, an accountant user has broad access to your financial data. They can view, edit, and reconcile transactions; run and customise reports; and use the accountant-only tools for cleanup and adjustments.


They can see everything in your books: bank transactions, invoices, bills, payroll figures if payroll is on, and all your reports. This is the access they need to keep the books accurate and prepare for taxes.


What they can't do by default is manage your subscription or billing or change the primary admin, unless you specifically transfer those rights. The primary admin role stays with you unless you hand it over.


## How many accountants can you add?


QuickBooks Online allows up to two accountant users on most plans, including Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus. The Advanced plan allows up to three.


This is usually plenty. One slot goes to your firm's lead accountant or bookkeeper, and the second can go to a team member who does the day-to-day work. If your firm needs more than two people in the file, they typically share access through the firm's own QuickBooks Online Accountant login rather than taking separate client slots.


## Fixing a missing Accounting Firms tab


The most common problem people hit is not seeing an Accounting Firms tab at all, only the option to add a regular user. This almost always comes down to one of two causes.


First, you may not be signed in as the primary admin. Only the primary admin and company admins see the accountant invite option. Check who holds the primary admin role and sign in under that account.


Second, you may be on QuickBooks Solopreneur, which doesn't support accountant users. To invite an accountant, you need to upgrade to Simple Start or a higher plan. This catches a lot of solo business owners who assumed any QBO plan would allow it.


## Removing or changing accountant access


You stay in control of access. If you switch accountants or end an engagement, you can remove access in a few clicks.


Go to Settings, then Manage Users, then the Accounting Firms tab. Find the accountant, select the dropdown in the Action column, and remove them. Their access ends immediately.


You can also resend an invitation if the first one didn't arrive or change which team member holds access. Reviewing who has access periodically is good practice, especially after staff changes on either side.


## After access: what happens next?


Giving your accountant access is step one. What matters is what they do with it. A good accountant will review your chart of accounts, check for miscategorised transactions, and set up a clean monthly workflow.


For firms, this invite is part of a larger[client onboarding process](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/onboarding-bookkeeping-clients) that includes connecting bank feeds and reviewing the books before the first close. Getting access is quick; setting up the books correctly is the real work.


Once access is set up, the recurring work begins: categorisation, reconciliation, and the[month-end close](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/quickbooks-month-end-close-automation) .


That's where automation earns its place.[Finlens](https://www.finlens.app/accountants) works inside the QBO file your accountant just gained access to, automating the mechanical parts of the close.


The time then goes to review instead of data entry. It sits alongside the other[QuickBooks automation tools](https://www.finlens.app/blogs/best-quickbooks-automation-tools) a modern firm runs.


## Conclusion


Giving your accountant access to QuickBooks Online is a quick task that unlocks the tools they need to keep your books accurate. Sign in as the primary admin, open Manage Users, use the Accounting Firms tab, and send the invite. Their status flips to Active once they accept, and they're in.


The two things that trip people up are the login role and the plan. If you don't see the Accounting Firms tab, you're either not signed in as the primary admin or you're on Solopreneur, which doesn't support accountant users. Fixing either one takes minutes.


Beyond the mechanics, remember that access is the start, not the finish. The value comes from what your accountant does with the books once they're in: cleaning up the chart of accounts, catching errors, and building a reliable monthly close. Grant the access, then let them get to the work that actually keeps your finances in order.


## Frequently asked questions


### How do I give my accountant access to QuickBooks Online?


Sign in as the primary admin, go to Settings, open Manage Users, select the Accounting Firms tab, enter your accountant's email, and send the invite. They accept through an emailed link, and their status changes from Invited to Active once they set up their login.


### Does adding an accountant count against my QuickBooks user limit?


No. Accountant users are added under the Accounting Firms tab and don't count toward your plan's standard user limit. This means you can invite an accountant without upgrading your plan or losing a regular user slot.


### How many accountants can I add to QuickBooks Online?


Most plans, including Simple Start, Essentials, and Plus, allow up to two accountant users. The Advanced plan allows up to three. Firms with larger teams usually share a single client slot through their own QuickBooks Online Accountant login rather than using multiple slots.


### Why can't I see the Accounting Firms tab?


The two common causes are not being signed in as the primary admin, and being on QuickBooks Solopreneur. Only the primary admin and company admins see the accountant invite option, and Solopreneur doesn't support accountant users at all. Upgrade to Simple Start or higher to invite one.


### What can my accountant see once I give them access?


An accountant user can view, edit, and reconcile all your financial transactions, run reports, and use accountant-only cleanup tools. They can see your full books, including bank activity, invoices, bills, and reports. By default they can't manage your subscription or billing unless you transfer those rights.


### Can my accountant do my taxes with QuickBooks access?


Access lets your accountant see and clean up the financial data they need to prepare your return, but the access itself is just to your books. Whether they file your taxes depends on your engagement with them, not on the QuickBooks permission.


### How do I remove an accountant from QuickBooks Online?


Go to Settings, then Manage Users, then the Accounting Firms tab. Find the accountant, open the dropdown in the Action column, and select Remove. Their access ends immediately. You can do this any time you switch accountants or end an engagement.


### My accountant didn't get the invite email. What do I do?


First, check that you entered their email address correctly, since a typo is the most common cause. Then go back to Manage Users and resend the invitation. Ask your accountant to check spam folders. If it still doesn't arrive, Intuit support can investigate a delivery issue.
